flags.headline: US-Iran conflict escalates to direct combat near the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend
flags.detail: US Central Command says US forces 'permanently disabled' two Iranian oil tankers and 'completely destroyed' another after Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps fired ballistic missiles toward a US aircraft carrier and destroyer patrolling near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran state media says it separately struck three additional tankers and several US-linked vessels in retaliation. Brent crude is up modestly (+0.6%) on the news as of Monday; the US equity market has not yet had a chance to react since it is closed today for Labor Day. This is a materially sharper escalation than the tanker-vs-tanker exchanges the desk tracked over the summer — it is now direct fire between US and Iranian forces. Directly relevant to the energy sleeve's shared key_risk (oil/gas price volatility) and to broader market risk sentiment heading into Tuesday's open.
flags.thesis_link: Matches the oil-and-gas-price-volatility key_risk shared by DVN, VLO, OKE, CVX and CNX (e.g. DVN key_risk: 'Oil and gas price volatility remains the dominant swing factor for earnings and free cash flow... could reverse quickly given global supply dynamics'). A supply-side shock at the world's most important oil chokepoint is a live test of that risk in both directions (price tailwind for the energy names, volatility risk for the broader book).

evidence.source: Al Jazeera — 'US, Iran engaged in tanker war: Where is the months-long conflict headed?'
ABC News — Iran live updates: US strikes oil tankers, Tehran claims attacks on US-linked vessels (CENTCOM statement)
